mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month signals a housing demand-driven divergence, where housing demand outpaces overall GDP growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to sector rotation into homebuilders.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% monthly change while GDPC1 < 0% monthly change
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS above 0.4% and UNRATE above 5.0% for two consecutive months signals strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% and UNRATE > 5.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable FEDFUNDS rate (< 0.75%) combined with a rising CPIAUCSL (> 2% YoY) for six months signals accommodative policy with rising inflation, eroding real corporate earnings and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.75% for six months AND CPIAUCSL > 2% YoY for six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 1% for three consecutive months signals rising household savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 1% monthly growth for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
